headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk: pipecat’s shared bus can ingest dbt outputs, while dbt can expose warehouse data into downstream voice/LLM flows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dbt-core can emit warehouse-derived text and pipecat has a shared bus/session model that can ingest upstream outputs. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if dbt artifacts or messages are treated as trusted content. The pairwise pathway is inferred from docs-only profiles, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF dbt output is forwarded into pipecat prompts or tool messages without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF the shared bus carries raw dbt artifacts, pipecat may parse attacker-controlled text as instructions.
mitigations: Add a strict content separator between dbt outputs and pipecat prompts.
Strip executable-looking directives from dbt-generated text before forwarding.
Require provenance tags on all bus messages.
Review one end-to-end message path for prompt-like content.
requires-engineering: implement schema validation on shared-bus payloads.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, and pipecat touches text, audio, video, images, and conversation state while supporting multiple instances on a shared bus. If warehouse-derived content is routed into pipecat, sensitive data can leak into downstream model calls or logs. The profiles do not prove default leakage, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF warehouse data is included in messages sent to pipecat, that data can enter conversation state.
IF pipecat forwards conversation state to external STT/LLM/TTS services, leakage expands beyond the original workspace.
mitigations: Minimize fields passed from dbt into pipecat.
Mask identifiers before any handoff.
Disable logging of message payloads for one test run.
Check which external services pipecat is configured to call.
requires-engineering: add DLP filtering on the bus.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have allowlisted network egress, but dbt-core only calls a data warehouse and pipecat is a multi-service voice framework with shared-bus concurrency. The profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same mutable resource, so a direct capability conflict is not established. Uncertainty remains, but the documented overlap is limited.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable backend, write conflicts may occur.
IF an orchestrator maps both to the same shared workspace, contention risk increases.
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces or service accounts.
Confirm only one agent writes to each mutable resource.
Run a quick lock test on the shared backend.
Document ownership of each API target.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency controls.

D_cascading_error.rationale: dbt-core can produce warehouse-derived outputs that pipecat may consume in real time, and pipecat has many downstream service integrations. If pipecat treats dbt output as authoritative, an upstream modeling error can cascade into spoken responses or automated actions. The profiles suggest the pathway but do not prove default trust, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF dbt output is used as a source of truth for pipecat prompts or actions, errors can propagate.
IF pipecat routes that output into LLM, TTS, or transport services, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before pipecat consumes dbt output.
Require human review for high-impact downstream actions.
Compare dbt outputs against a known-good baseline.
Limit pipecat to read-only presentation of dbt results.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core is documented as touching data warehouse data, while pipecat touches conversation state and can call many third-party AI services. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is explicitly documented, so only a low compliance concern is supportable. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise data flow, not a single-agent violation.
conditions: IF regulated warehouse data is forwarded into pipecat services, residency or retention obligations may be implicated.
IF pipecat is configured with external vendors lacking the needed DPA, compliance gaps emerge.
mitigations: Inventory which data classes cross the boundary.
Check vendor DPAs for each external service.
Disable retention where possible for one session.
Keep regulated data out of voice workflows.
requires-engineering: formalize residency and retention controls.
